note: TOWNS, FARM AND SOCIAL ADDENDUM (2026-10-14), work packages. The editor's merge of the four design3 tracks (farm N, towns T, social S, integration I) into ONE consistent set: 32 new packages, one amendment per existing package (RT1..RT37, the 71 track amendments merged and deduplicated), disjoint ownership proven by check_ownership.py over ALL layers (owners.json + feature addendum + design_ui + design2 + this file). Addendum to PLAN_2D.md, PLAN_2D_FEATURES.md and the dungeon addendum; where they differ this file and ADDENDUM.md win (DT1). Wave '5b' sits between 5 and 6, '3b' between 3 and 4. Every task ends '-> verify: <named check>'. Amendments to BUILT packages (built: true) are fix-round tasks executed by the lead before wave 4 in the order of RT1..RT9.

decisions.title: One addendum, one package file, a clear precedence
decisions.decision: This addendum and design3/FINAL/packages.json are binding for the towns, the treetop farm, the citizens and the social sim. They override PLAN_2D.md / PLAN_2D_FEATURES.md where they differ, they never override design2's dungeon addendum (zone graph, floors, loot, v2 cast and city) or design_ui's navigation spec except for the repairs listed in DT33 and the cross-track fixes DT14-DT16. The four track documents stay as reference (docs/design/towns_farm_social/).
decisions.why: Four designers worked in parallel on one codebase; the editor merged them and every disagreement is in section 11.

decisions.title: Tiers and gates
decisions.decision: CORE = needed for the first playable town loop (gate G5b); EXTENDED = content and polish that can be dropped without touching a CORE gate; LATER = optional and built last (S-marriage only); QA = acceptance packages of wave 7 (hard dependencies on CORE packages only, softDependsOn for the optional ones: a dropped package makes its checks SKIP with the capability name, never fail). The loop gates are G4 (wave-4 content), G5, G5b (first playable town loop), G6, G7 (design_integration 3.4).
decisions.why: design_integration 3.4; the three tracks used different words (scope / class): normalised to `class`.

decisions.title: The user's six requirements are all IN; marriage-style is scheduled, not hoped for
decisions.decision: Requirement (3) names marriage-style relationships. They are the LATER tier (S-marriage, wave 6) because they depend on the vocabulary decision Q2, but the package is in the plan, has an owner, tests, copy files, and every hook it needs is a late-bound task of built or earlier packages. If Q2 is not answered the defaults of the brief are used (bedste ven -> hjertven -> forlovet -> gift; items Hjertebuket and Løfteagern).
decisions.why: The user's requirement list; design_social 9.

decisions.title: The zone graph and the spawn names
decisions.decision: farm (Min Trækronsgård) -- ONE hanging bridge -- traetoppen (the treetop city, a levelled builder, zone traetoppen) -- ONE bridge -- hyggebyen (a grid map, zone id `city`). The Skovport is REMOVED (v2, generator and experience v2 agree); a sign SIGN_FARM_FOREST stands where the gate was. Spawns: farm {default, from_home, from_traetoppen}, hyggebyen {default, from_traetoppen, 14 x from_int_<building>}, traetoppen {default, from_farm, from_hyggebyen, from_skovlift}, interiors {default; exit from_int_<building> in the outer area}. The only warp of the farm is the bridge to traetoppen:from_farm.
decisions.why: design_farm DN2, design_towns 3.1, design2 DV2; farm_probe B8-B10 (43 checks).

decisions.title: farm.map is N01's (carve-out from P11)
decisions.decision: data/maps/farm.map, localization/farm_signs.csv, tests/sections/maps_farm.gd and tools/farm/** belong to N01-farm-map (wave 4). P11 keeps hyggebyen.map, areas.csv and maps_iso.gd. To undo: delete one `owns` entry of N01 and the P11 ownsRemove of RT12; N01's tasks become P11 tasks with the same text.
decisions.why: The farm map is a design of its own with its own validator; both packages are wave 4.

decisions.title: Five farm stages, derived and never saved
decisions.decision: Stage = f(home_tier): Spiren 1-2, Kvisten 3-4, Grenen 5-7 (+1 growth row), Kronen 8-9 (+2), Slottet 10 (+3), data in lua/config/farm_site.lua, FarmStage.of_tier(tier) -> {id, index, rows}; the world flag farm_stage (1..5) is a mirror. Anchor contract: the `home` marker is the DOOR cell, anchor = iso_center + (-32, 19); the 9 x 3 deck base plus three void growth rows hold every tier's footprint and keep from_home free (probe C5-C7, mutant caught).
decisions.why: design_farm 4.2-4.3.

decisions.title: Farm objects: expansion, bin, shed, pond, greenhouse
decisions.decision: The field expansion is a marker (field_expansion id= cells= price=800) + UiConfirm, unlocked through the PUBLIC IsoArea API only (P04 needs no edit), persisted as the area flag zone_east. The shipping bin has no UI of its own: E ships the whole selected hotbar stack (crop / product / forage), paid at day_started at pay_ratio 1.0 (the seed shop's price: a convenience, never an arbitrage; the ratio is a data knob). The tool shed emits open_home_chest. The pond is decorative (no fishing). The greenhouse (N07) is OPTIONAL and gated on Q1; the default is NO and the 4 x 3 slot stays a silent data marker.
decisions.why: design_farm 5-6; income model: typical player 328 g/day on day 28, never needs more than 84 plots.

decisions.title: The first morning is data, run by a 100-line runner
decisions.decision: A new game starts at 06:00 on day 1: Pip (a TEMPORARY Npc2D at post pip_mailbox), Fekongens letter (P14's text), Pip's goodbye, the auto-accepted quest forste_dage (till 3, sow 3, water 3, mail on day 2, harvest 1; 150 g + 10 carrot seeds + 3 fertilizer + Pip +1), ten once-per-save whisper hints. Esc skips; `farm_tutorial.first_morning.enabled = false` falls back to P14's letter-only flow; never on Continue. The towns' routine keeps Pip in town on day 1 (day_max 1), so there is never a second Pip.
decisions.why: design_farm 11; integration leg L00 rewritten around it.

decisions.title: The roster is 30 citizens: 23 CORE, 7 EXTENDED
decisions.decision: 15 existing + 7 design2 cast (Hoppe, Brumme, Pip, Sofus, Fru Ugle, Natteblik, Birk) + 8 new from unused talk-capable bodies (rasmus, lamplighter_kiki, bertil, bodil, innkeeper_kvak, cub_bamse, clerk_fjerpen, fiddler_strimmel). CORE = the 15, the 7 and Skriver Fjerpen (23); EXTENDED = the other 7 (their npcs.lua rows are V1's, so the roster is 30 either way). The hero twins are rasmus, lamplighter_kiki, bertil, bodil: absent while the player is that hero; Birk and Kløvermynte (also playable) are never absent because the seed shop needs its keeper. A look cap of 16 distinct visuals per area; routines are validated to a planned peak of 14.
decisions.why: design_towns 5.1; design_integration 5.4.

decisions.title: Presence is a pure function of the clock
decisions.decision: Routines.where_is(npc, ctx) over Lua registry data with walking times from a baked route table (data/towns/routes.json): no simulation, no saved NPC positions, sleeping and skipping cost nothing. The TownDirector of the area the player is in keeps exactly the wanted citizens alive and frees every node on area exit.
decisions.why: design_towns 6: 7-9 us per call, 0.045 ms per physics frame for a whole day in Hyggebyen.

decisions.title: NpcDirector is a STATIC facade; the late-binding form is fixed
decisions.decision: There is no NpcDirector autoload. Every consumer (S-core, D2's hub marker, the loop's TownProbe) binds it the same way: Svc.node("NpcDirector") first (test fakes), then Svc.static_call("res://scripts/towns/npc_director.gd", &"<method>", [args], <default>). Methods: is_absent, is_away, is_present, where_is, population, resync(npc_id := ""). The when= grammar gains at:<npc> and away:<npc>; the hourly game_event routine_changed {hour} refreshes them.
decisions.why: design_towns X4; S-core patched (b1).

decisions.title: Opening hours live in the buildings registry, one rule
decisions.decision: Hours.state(building, ctx) is the ONLY rule: the door (Door2D), ShopSystem.is_open (a late-bound hook, RT5), the closing sequence (ShopHours) and the festival closure (SocialManager.shop_closed_by_festival) all read it. Hours are NOT fields of the shop defs (a building may host no shop; four packages own shop defs). Each shop is closed on exactly one weekday; 7-10 of 10 shops are open at noon on every day.
decisions.why: design_towns X1, design_integration X13.

decisions.title: Stores are walk-in rooms built from data
decisions.decision: 24 rooms (14 CORE, 10 EXTENDED) from data/interiors/<core|ext>/int_<id>.json by ONE builder (InteriorRoom), a 7-line stub map each (@projection iso, @zone <outer zone>, @builder), a 3x1 counter band (invisible hatch bars stop the player, citizens pass), the keeper one row behind, the `shop` interactable in front; E opens P18's panel over the live room (guide section 07). Pieces resolve: baked kit manifest > furniture.json > stand-ins > placeholder.
decisions.why: design_towns 4; 6.2 ms mean build, flood fill passes in all 24 rooms.

decisions.title: Cross-track fix: the dress marker reads the flag `festival_now`
decisions.decision: The farm map wrote `dress event=festival_today`; the social contract has the METHOD festival_today() and the WORLD FLAG festival_now (id of the festival active now, empty otherwise). N01's lifted map is changed in this ONE place and N05 re-evaluates on town_festival_started / _ended.
decisions.why: A flag nobody writes would have left the bunting off forever (found by comparing the three contracts).

decisions.title: Cross-track fix: Pip counts as met after the first morning
decisions.decision: farm_intro_pip declares social = false and ends through the normal Npc2D path, so SocialManager.on_conversation_finished('postman_pip', ...) counts it; the real Pip of the routines never greets the player as a stranger a second time.
decisions.why: Without it the scripted scene and the social first-meeting line would both introduce him.

decisions.title: Cross-track fix: a citizen without a dialogue file can still be talked to
decisions.decision: 4 of the 15 existing citizens and the 8 new ones have no lua/dialogue module. Npc2D passes an empty module to DialogueBridge.decorate, which always returns a greeting, the social choices and a close choice (P14 + S-talk tasks).
decisions.why: S-talk appended its choices 'before the Lua close choice': with no module there was no close choice.

decisions.title: SocialManager is the ONLY writer of friendship; the sixth feature autoload
decisions.decision: Autoload SocialManager (scripts/social/social_manager.gd), save section `social` (order 60, after loot 40 / dungeon 45 / collection 50), friend_<npc> and friend_last_<npc> become a derived mirror rewritten after every change and every load; reset() re-seeds points from the flags (hearts x 100), so quests, loot gifts, dialogue Lua and old saves keep working. Registered by add_autoload.py (sanctioned edit E1) after the P01 / F1 fix-round widened the closed lists of five.
decisions.why: design_social DS1, DS32; measured in the clone: 59 of 59 check_project checks pass with the patch.

decisions.title: The social rules are design_social's DS1-DS36
decisions.decision: Adopted whole: hearts 0-10 (100 points, half heart at 50), the first FINISHED conversation of a Monday-Sunday week gives exactly one heart (the DF3 floor), no decay and nothing negative, gifts 40 / 20 / 8 / 0 / 0 with rarity x1.25 / x1.5, birthday x4, 1 per day and 2 per week, 30 distinct birthdays (min gap 2, none on or beside a festival), nine festivals + the wedding, six activity primitives, heart events started by the player, the marriage ladder with no gender gate and no break-up, FNV-1a + fmix32 over a saved seed, state queries instead of edge triggers, daily work deferred and coalesced. Monte Carlo (200 runs x 336 days): a typical player reaches 8 hearts with a tier A citizen on day 72 (p10 55, p90 97).
decisions.why: design_social 2, 13; social_scripts/mc_result*.json.

decisions.title: One generic Lua kind for the new data: `registry`
decisions.decision: routines, buildings, events and festivals are registries (kind = "registry", get_registry / get_registry_entry): ONE P10 fix-round (RT4) serves the towns and the social track; the social track's dedicated-kinds patch stays a fallback only.
decisions.why: design_social C2 / RC3; proven with 102 scripts, 0 lint findings.

decisions.title: Zero new EventBus signals, one new input action
decisions.decision: Everything new is EventBus.game_event(name, payload) (section 8.2); friend_changed(npc_id, hearts) keeps its arity and fires only on whole hearts; the one new action is `people` = P (pad: pause row 'Folk'). core.signal_contract_exact stays at 75.
decisions.why: design_social DS29, design_integration 6.3-6.4.

decisions.title: Six new screens or surfaces, each with a registry row and a baseline owner
decisions.decision: people, gift, calendar (journal tab), social_hud, event_overlay, post. Rows live in tests/lib/ui_screens.d/{social,social_events,towns}.json (one file, one owner; UiAudit.screens() merges the directory), each baseline PNG is owned by its screen's package. The People book is read-only and lists only citizens the player has met; the friendship glyph is a heart with a moss sprout, distinct from the health hearts by SHAPE.
decisions.why: UI_NAVIGATION.md; design_social 11.

decisions.title: Festival posts: ONE marker per spot, the city has a sidecar
decisions.decision: Hyggebyen carries ONE `post set=fest spot=hyggetorv` marker (24 posts at fixed offsets); the three city spots (torvet, badehus, raadhus) are `fest_sets` of data/towns/traetoppen.json (T-routes, wave 5; built by T-director). The social track's 24 per-post marker lines in P11 / V4 are dropped. The names fest_<spot>_host / judge / stall_1..4 / table_1..2 / gather_1..16 are the contract.
decisions.why: design_towns X2; the city has no map text.

decisions.title: ONE decor mechanism: I5's FestivalDecor
decisions.decision: Festival decoration is placed by I5's data-driven FestivalDecor (late-bound from the TownDirector) for Hyggebyen AND the city; the shipped maps carry no `when=fest:<id>` decor markers (the grammar still allows a hand-placed one). EXTENDED: without I5 the festival works and the town is plain.
decisions.why: design_integration 5.3: social's marker decor cannot reach the city.

decisions.title: The night watch is the director's; world_2d.gd needs only D0's edits
decisions.decision: At 23:30 a whisper, at 23:45 the night watch sends the player to farm:from_home (held during modals; off on the farm and in homes). It lives in the TownDirector, so no P04 edit is needed, and it coexists with D0's pass-out relocation. The extra world_2d.gd tasks are D0's: the warm-clips rule R-V4 (walkers warm `walk`) and the pass-out wake (DT50).
decisions.why: design_towns X10 against design_integration X4.

decisions.title: Festivals, shops and the bed
decisions.decision: A festival window ends by 23:00 (the pass-out is at 24:00); while it is active SocialManager keeps the config override time.sleep_from_hour = to and RE-APPLIES it from the state query on every flush, load, area change and festival event (GameManager.set_config_override is a never-saved test seam wiped by clear_config_overrides()), closes shops per the festival's `closes` / `stays_open`, and gathers citizens through override_for. Festivals ignore weather (no rain venue: honest stub).
decisions.why: design_social DS17, DS28.

decisions.title: Shop friendliness is tiny and visible
decisions.decision: 1 point per 100 gold spent (weekly cap 10 per keeper) and a weekly keeper sample from the hearts the shop def names; the existing friend_discount (0.005 per heart, F4's PriceCurve) is untouched, but PriceCurve reads the KEEPER's hearts.
decisions.why: design_social DS23.

decisions.title: Copy: a review state machine, a lint, the `_V` voice rule
decisions.decision: Every new CSV is delivered at status draft, a fresh-context agent sets ai_reviewed in the same wave, native_reviewed is only ever set by a commit of the user. Voiced rows end in `_V` (<= 14 words, no digits, no %), the generated lua/dialogue/_voiced_social.lua indexes them for the existing hash lint, 8 archetype presets give 30 citizens their pitch and rate, voice is generated only for rows at ai_reviewed or better. Style sheet R1-R11 and copy_lint C1-C10 (I1).
decisions.why: design_integration 4.

decisions.title: Audio: an AudioDirector child, a cue log, synthesised placeholders
decisions.decision: AudioManager stays the only audio autoload and creates the AudioDirector as a child; data in lua/config/audio.lua maps area / surface / event to cue ids; every call is logged in AudioManager.cue_log (ring of 256) so headless tests assert hooks without files; placeholders are synthesised in Python and replaced by dropping real files of the same name. P24 is the heaviest package of wave 6 (size L, seam for a split in RT31).
decisions.why: design_integration 4.5.

decisions.title: Art: three kits, a split with P22, S3TC for the farm kit
decisions.decision: N03 bakes only the 10 farm-only props, 3 backdrops and the field_grass terrain; P22 bakes coop_small, barn_small, animal_house, paw_prints, apple_tree, bench, signpost to the contract sizes and gets the 16 props_extra rows. I3 (CORE, 35 pieces: counter band, sign bracket, the 16 pieces the 14 core rooms draw as stand-ins, 15 emblems), I4 (EXTENDED, 69 dressing pieces placed by overlays), I5 (EXTENDED, 24 festival pieces + FestivalDecor). N03 imports its kit VRAM-compressed (65.5 -> 15.8 MB). The apple-tree season variants are an optional lookup of the node handler's owner.
decisions.why: design_farm 10, design_integration 5.1-5.6.

decisions.title: Budgets
decisions.decision: Process VRAM <= 400 MB (city peak 307.9 MB with the S3TC farm kit, 357.6 without); 16 distinct NPC visuals per area (8.93 MB each); interior <= 130 nodes, <= 12 ms warm rebuild, <= 4 lights; city <= 40 ms build / <= 6 ms frame; the FARM has its own row (< 60 ms build, <= 8 ms frame, <= 560 / 640 / 780 draw calls at zoom 0.4 / 0.3 / 0.2, <= 130 MB, <= 12 lights) because its 1,206-cell y-sorted ground cannot be 94 calls; citizens <= 0.4 ms per frame; save <= 60 KB.
decisions.why: design_integration 5.6-5.7, design_farm 14.2.

decisions.title: ONE data-only extension proof
decisions.decision: I2's leg L18 (copy the repo to a temp project, add only the data files of tests/fixtures/town/**): citizen, building (a new walk-in shop), routine edit, shop hours, festival, heart event, quest, and zero .gd / .tscn changed. zz_towns and zz_social re-run their legs; the P25 how-tos use the same fixture files.
decisions.why: The proof was promised three times (T-qa, S-qa, L18).

decisions.title: Four QA packages, one index
decisions.decision: N08 (farm), T-qa (towns), S-qa (social) each own their section, shots and report; I6 owns the aggregate (rows 31-39, the three-hero windowed run, the budget table) and links the three. QA packages never hard-depend on an EXTENDED package.
decisions.why: check_ownership.py D flagged T-qa and I6 (CORE with hard dependencies on EXTENDED).

decisions.title: Repairs of design_ui's ownership (not this addendum's design)
decisions.decision: check_ownership.py (raw mode) found 34 pattern overlaps and 13 tracked files with two owners in the merged table, all caused by design_ui and none by a design3 package: P07 still owns the component files design_ui gave to P28 and P17 and localization/ui.csv (P14), and P27's docs/qa/** still matches every screen baseline PNG. RT7 and RT34 list the exact paths. Everything else of design_ui stands.
decisions.why: check_ownership.py --raw output (section 15).

decisions.title: One fix-round before wave 4, in this order
decisions.decision: RT1 P15 (save registry tests), RT2 F1 (autoload tool, FEATURE_NODES, Grant), RT3 P01 (check_project six names, the `people` action, the docs copies and the new header line), RT4 P10 (registry kind + 4 api functions), RT5 P12 (shop hours hook), RT6 P04 (when= delegate), RT7 P07 (SCREEN_ORDER + the ownership repair), RT8 P09 (--fast, ui_screens.d merge, DEVELOPMENT.md), RT9 P03 (E2). Each is a task of a BUILT package executed by the lead; late binding makes every one harmless before its consumer exists; new checks go into a section of the amended package itself (DT58).
decisions.why: design_social 15.4, design_towns 10.2.

decisions.title: Three sanctioned shared edits: E1, E2, E3
decisions.decision: See section 8.14.
decisions.why: E1 existed; E2 and E3 are the new routine chores.

decisions.title: The wave plan keeps the tracks' waves; the load is stated, not hidden
decisions.decision: Wave 4 = 65 points, wave 5 = 62, 5b = 27, 6 = 28, 7 = 15 (S=1, M=2, L=3, XL=4). S-core, T-towns-core and N01 cannot slide out of wave 4 (wave-5 packages depend on them). If a wave overruns: stagger writers inside the wave (data and copy last), then defer in this order: I4 sets, I5, N05 / N06, T-ext-content, S-heart-content, S-fest-content, S-marriage, T-post-office, T-greetings. CORE is never deferred; the gates list what they skip.
decisions.why: design_integration 7.1 and 7.4; section 9.

decisions.title: Honest dependency: F2 / F6's friend hooks live only with S-marriage
decisions.decision: SocialManager.partner_in_home / pick_visitor / start_house_party (the weekly guest gift naming a friend, the tier-8 party with friends, the partner in the room) are provided by S-marriage. Without it HomeManager.guests_today() is [] and the visitor gift stays anonymous.
decisions.why: design_social 14.1: the three methods are marked S-marriage.

decisions.title: Small questions are decided here and are data knobs
decisions.decision: Shipping bin ratio 1.0 (farm_site.bin.pay_ratio); the pond stays decoration; a home opens while its owner is home and awake and friend_<npc> >= 1; the mayor commutes Tue-Thu (78 game minutes each way); the inn sells nothing; the `Hvor er ...?` list is built in wave 6 and droppable; the festival music is a synthesised placeholder; festivals hold the bed until they end; the key is P; the two stalls (Torvestanden, Natteblik-vinduet) keep an outdoor counter and have NO room (the sketch's own form: the one deviation from the literal requirement 4, asked as Q7). Each is one data value or one input-map line.
decisions.why: None of them changes a contract; the build follows these values unless the user says otherwise.

decisions.title: The plan header gains a NEW line; the pinned line never moves
decisions.decision: RT3 copies the addendum and the package file into docs/design/ and adds ONE new header line to PLAN_2D.md (design2 does the same); the SUPERSEDE_LINE pin of check_project.gd uses `contains`, so no existing line is rewritten.
decisions.why: design_social RC9 / design_integration X7 wanted ONE rewrite of line 3 plus the pin; a new line needs neither.

decisions.title: The retired town name is never written
decisions.decision: Not in this addendum, not in packages.json, not in any task; the lint source writes it in two halves like check_project.gd does. check_ownership.py has no way to check this, so build_final.py scrubs and asserts.
decisions.why: p01.design_files_use_current_town_name would fail on the first copy.

decisions.title: The hero id is derived, not stored
decisions.decision: hero = CharacterCatalog.hero_of_skin(GameManager.character_skin).id (rasmus, kiki, kloevermynte, birk, bertil, bodil), read late bound by the routine context; the world flag hero_id is a test override nobody writes in play.
decisions.why: The towns prototype read a flag that no package wrote.

decisions.title: Natteblik has two stands (honest wart)
decisions.decision: Design2 puts him beside the Hulen of floors 2 / 6 / 10 at night entry, the towns put him at the city's bat window 19:30-23:30. One shop id, so the hours rule closes both outside 20:00-23:30; the two places are different areas and the dungeon's clock is paused.
decisions.why: Not reconciled further: it is a bat.

decisions.title: Package size honesty
decisions.decision: P14 grows from L to XL (the NPC runtime serves six tracks), P24 from M to L. Both are single-owner files; the seams for a split are written down (RT24, RT31). Every NEW package is one agent's job (largest: I4 XL, 69 art pieces, droppable set by set).
decisions.why: design_integration R11.

decisions.title: A decision-gated package contributes only conditional amendments
decisions.decision: N07 is `optional: true`; its two changes of built packages (P06: indoor flag + crops_extra merge) are `conditional` tasks of RT11 that exist only if the lead activates N07; its winter seeds have their own shop file so the seed shop's hours cannot block winter planting.
decisions.why: design_farm 5.5 and Q1; the carve-out of P12's glob for lua/shops/greenhouse_seeds.lua is N07's own owns line.

decisions.title: The farm's post names are the contract
decisions.decision: pip_mailbox, hoppe_fence, bench_a, porch, field_edge. The social draft's `farm.visitor_bench` is not a post: nobody uses it.
decisions.why: design_towns X5.

decisions.title: Who attends a festival
decisions.decision: The citizens whose home area is the festival's area (an absent hero twin excluded), ordered by SocialRng.roll(seed, [festival, npc]), at most 15 plus the host (the look cap is 16, so the crowd never drops anybody), one per fest_<spot>_gather_<n>; keepers of `stays_open` shops stay at their shop; attendance points go to the host and to every citizen the player TALKED to during the window.
decisions.why: design_social 7.8 and design_towns X6; S-core's task text said 'tier A/B friends sorted by id' and no cap.

decisions.title: A `routine = true` citizen is placed by the director ONLY where a director controls the area
decisions.decision: V1 sets `routine = true` on all 30 npcs.lua rows in wave 4, but T-director lands in wave 5b. The P14 `npc` marker handler therefore skips such a row only when NpcDirector.controls(npc_id, area) is true (the citizen has a routine entry AND the area is under a director: a `town` marker whose handler exists, or the city with its sidecar and `city_town.gd`); before that the static marker NPCs of Hyggebyen and the city keep talking, so gate G5 (L03 talk, L06 dialogue entry) has somebody to talk to.
decisions.why: Found tracing the loop: with a flag-only skip waves 5 and 5b would have shown empty towns while G5 requires a conversation.

decisions.title: The room services have marker rows
decisions.decision: Rooms place V6's PostBox2D, NoticeBoard2D and BathTub2D from room JSON markers through IsoArea.resolve_handler, which reads lua/config/marker_handlers.lua. design2 registered only `mailbox` (V4's builder instantiated the other two in the city); RT19 now registers `bath` and `board` too (scripts/traetoppen/life/{bath_tub_2d,notice_board_2d}.gd), and V4's city JSON carries none of the three.
decisions.why: Found tracing the loop: without the rows the Rådhus board and the bathhouse tub stay announcing counters.

decisions.title: A door of an unbuilt EXTENDED building is a clean locked nameplate
decisions.decision: P11's hyggebyen.map carries 14 door markers, four of them for EXTENDED buildings (the king's house, the mayor's house, Pippin's house, Birk's hives) whose registry rows live in T-ext-content's lua/buildings/ext.lua. Door2D treats a building without a registry row as a locked nameplate labelled BLD_<ID> (towns.csv defines all 30 names), so dropping T-ext-content leaves four locked doors, never a broken one.
decisions.why: design_towns proved the CORE-only data green (20 buildings) but not the map's doors.

decisions.title: The 24:00 pass-out wakes at home
decisions.decision: world_2d.gd's `_sleep_sequence(true)` leaves the player where he stands (a shop, a street, the far end of the field). The farm design (6.4) and the loop leg l11_pass_out_wakes_on_farm assume farm:from_home; D0 (the owner of world_2d.gd) already writes the gentle defeat that wakes there, so its amendment (RT22) gets the pass-out as a second small task (no gold loss, no run end).
decisions.why: Found tracing leg L11: three tracks promised the wake position, none wrote it.

decisions.title: A named post is found through the NpcDirector facade
decisions.decision: The festival runtime (S-events) and the event marks need the position of fest_<spot>_host / gather_<n> / mark:<id>. Hyggebyen has them as map markers, the city only in the sidecar, so both ask NpcDirector.post_ground(area_id, name) (T-routes' facade, forwarded to the live TownDirector); I5's FestivalDecor is handed the director and calls director.post_ground(name) directly.
decisions.why: Found tracing the festival leg: the social design assumed `find_markers("post")`, which is empty in the city.

decisions.title: Every game event of the contract is named by its emitter
decisions.decision: A contract row is only kept when the emitting package's tasks name the event and every consumer that is not a test is a package whose tasks read it; `counter_used` (named by no task and read by nobody) was dropped, routine_changed was added to T-director, home_exterior_ready to N02 and N05.
decisions.why: Found by a script comparing the 26 contract rows with the 228 task texts.

decisions.title: Every counter has three kinds of host, so a keeper can always be talked to
decisions.decision: A counter band carries the centre host of its service (`shop`, `post_counter`, `bath`, `board`, `appraisal`) and TWO `talk` hosts (ellipse 40 x 22) on the customer cells m-1 and m+1 in front of the counter ENDS; the builder yard adds a `desk` host (game_event open_home_builder {tier}) as the second door of the Husbyggeri; the two stalls get the same trio from the `counters` rows of the city sidecar. The BUILT E-query (circle r = 45 at the facing cell, the host nearest to the PLAYER wins) then decides by where the player stands: the middle cell opens the panel, an end cell opens the keeper's own dialogue (greeting, weekly heart, gifts, topics, birthdays, quest offers and turn-ins, the upgrade choice). A talk host stays disabled while no keeper stands in the room. The ShopCounter seam `forward_to_keeper` and its rule 'a giftable hotbar item takes E first' are REMOVED (the rule would have sent 12 of 12 tools and 8 of 8 seeds into a gift talk instead of the shop panel).
decisions.why: Reviewers (social_economy, plan): with the built rule the keeper was selected 0 of 576 samples (counter 144 at the default radius), 15 of 23 CORE citizens are keepers whose outdoor presence is 0-2 h a day for Natteblik, Sofus, Brumme, Pip, Zephyr, 14 of 24 quests have a keeper as giver, and the home ladder (74,000 g) was reachable only through Hasselnød's dialogue. Proof: replay and REAL Player stub agree on 23,760 samples of the 14 core layouts, A 252 / 252, B 126 / 126, C 0 (D3/final_editor/se1/out); availability Monte Carlo, typical tier A to 8 hearts with visits at mixed hours: day 69 / p90 154 / 10 % never WITHOUT the cells, day 70 / p90 108 / 0 % never WITH them (se6).

decisions.title: A lifted file names no class of a later wave
decisions.decision: Every lifted prototype script is EDITED so that it names no class_name owned by a later wave: Hours has its own clock-only now_ctx() (Routines.now_ctx extends it later), Door2D and ShopHours reach Routines only through Svc.static_call with a safe default (homes locked, no eviction by owner), NpcDirector tracks live directors as Objects in its static registry and makes duck-typed calls (no `as TownDirector`), SocialManager reaches GiftRules only through Svc.static_call. Each of the four packages carries a check (`no_forward_class_refs`) that scans its own scripts for the identifiers of later packages outside strings and comments; towns_data also loads its scripts in a tree without the later files.
decisions.why: The package-level 'no forward dependencies' proof does not see class_name references. Measured by simulating each wave: hours.gd alone 'Parse Error: Identifier "Routines" not declared', npc_director.gd 'Could not find type "TownDirector"', social_manager.gd 'Failed to instantiate an autoload' (three GiftRules references).

decisions.title: The opening-hours rule has ONE test switch and a stated clock
decisions.decision: The config key `towns.hours_enabled` (default true) makes Hours.shop_open answer null; P12's helper `ShopHoursGate` honours it, so shop_system.gd gains no third `static_call(` line and the built pin economy.late_binding_via_svc stays true. Which clock a section runs at: sections that are NOT about hours run with the switch off (economy.gd's `_fresh()` since design2 gave that file to DL1: RT35; every later section that buys or sells sets it in its fixture), sections about hours (towns_data, towns_interiors*, towns_director, economy_hours, the shop panel's closed state, the hour legs of town_loop) leave it on and set the clock explicitly through LoopClock / t.set_time (Monday 12:00 unless the check names another). The built economy section is edited by DL1's amendment, not by P12's fix-round.
decisions.why: Measured in a clone: with the buildings registry loaded all 9 shops are closed at the new-game clock (day 1, 06:00, Monday), 25 built P12 checks fail; with the switch off economy runs 304 checks, 0 failed, and core + save + data + content_features + economy 1,104 checks, 0 failed (D3/final_editor/te2).

decisions.title: The city sidecar and LevelNav belong to T-routes; unbuilt rooms are PENDING
decisions.decision: T-routes (wave 5) owns data/towns/traetoppen.json (doors, 36 posts, gates, festival spots, the two stall counters) and scripts/towns/level_nav.gd and depends on V3-levels (levels_graph(), RT21), so the route table bakes the CITY in wave 5; T-director (5b) only builds the Door2Ds and stall counters from it (city_town.gd) and re-checks the door coordinates against V4's geometry. The 14 CORE rooms are data of T-interiors-core (same wave): TownsValidate.PENDING_AREAS lists an unbuilt room by name as SKIP and the wave-5 gate requires the list to be empty. The marker collection and the post snap (TownMarks.collect / resolve_cells, lifted from the prototype's town_marker.gd) are T-routes' own statics.
decisions.why: Simulated wave-5 acceptance without the city: routines.feasible FAIL (219 findings), routines.places_exist FAIL (81), post_capacity FAIL; the acceptance of T-routes could not be met in its own wave.

decisions.title: The G5b closure holds no dungeon-track package except D0 and DR7
decisions.decision: V4-city-map no longer depends on D2-dungeon-floors and P19-forest-combat (RT29: removeDependsOn; P19 becomes a softDependsOn); its two chain checks SKIP with the capability `D2 landed` and are REQUIRED by DQ's E1 / E2 (wave 7). The hard-dependency closure of the 16 CORE packages plus V4 is 49 packages, 34 unbuilt (47 plus D0 and DR7; checker section I prints it and fails on any dungeon-track member except D0 and DR7, which the loop needs: the pass-out wake and the stall shop natteblik_maps). A sequencing rule: packages outside the closure (wardrobe A2 / F5 / F8, D1, D2, DR*, D3, DL1-DL6, P19, V8 / V9, P23) start after G5b or run in a separate lane.
decisions.why: closure.py: the closure of d3 CORE + V4 was 52 packages, 37 unbuilt, containing D1, D2, DR0, DR1 and P19 (12 points) only through two edges used by two chain tests and two planter node kinds; about 54 of 155 points of waves 4-5b are outside the closure.

decisions.title: A fix-round amendment writes only into its own section and names only checks that exist at that time
decisions.decision: Each fix-round task of a BUILT package (RT1-RT9) puts new checks into a section file of its own package (ownsAdd: RT4 tests/sections/data_registry.gd, RT5 tests/sections/economy_hours.gd, RT9 tests/sections/loc_towns.gd, P26 loc_final.gd) or keeps an EXISTING check green, and names no check of a section owned by a later wave (checker section J fails on it): RT2 builds its pristine project inside the tool and leaves content_features.gd alone, the three social.* checks of RT2 / RT4 are S-core's, RT8's merge check is in P09's ui_audit section. Checks that need a later package are proven by that package at its own gate.
decisions.why: review/plan/out/verify_cross_owner.txt: 21 task / check pairs named sections owned by wave 4-5 packages (and the layered ownership gate would have flagged the edits as FOREIGN).

decisions.title: Uglehulen is a service: no shop id, a counter of kind `appraisal`
decisions.decision: The building row of Uglehulen has no `shop` field (kind service); her room's centre host emits game_event open_appraisal {npc, building} (design2's event, hosted by F4's LootService, screen DL7), is refused with the closed whisper while Hours.state is closed and whispers COUNTER_APPRAISE_SOON while LootService has no appraise(); her talk cells open her dialogue with the choice 'Vurdér mine fund'. The draft shop id fru_ugle_vurdering is removed from the registry, the room wiring, T-greetings (11 shop ids, 61 rows) and section 8.12.
decisions.why: design2's final addendum says the id does not exist (DX57); a ShopCounter on it called ShopSystem.open_shop on an unknown id and the validators that require every building shop id to exist could not pass.

decisions.title: A gift of value asks first; progress is protected
decisions.decision: S-gifts hides tools in the hotbar, the last copy of any tool, the materials of the next home tier and the pieces of a wardrobe set whose capstone is open (late bound reads of F2 / F4), and GiftRules.needs_confirm marks tools, rarity rare and sell value >= 100 g; the picker opens UiConfirm (default focus Fortryd) for those, cheap gifts stay one press.
decisions.why: social_dump.json: all 12 tools, 56 rare items (sell 34-1,670 g) and all 26 building materials were giftable, one press gave the item away for at most 60 points.

decisions.title: Four economy guards
decisions.decision: (a) A partner who keeps a shop leaves the farmhouse at opens - walk x 2 / 60 - 5 minutes (Maja has no morning there, Kløvermynte until 06:48, Brumme and Rasmus 06:56), validated for the 11 candidates by hours.keeper_covers_hours with a partner overlay; (b) contest rewards are capped in value by SocialValidator SV14 (first <= min(2 x the cheapest winning entry, 400 g), second <= 0.7 x first, third <= 0.4 x first); (c) a festival lists a shop in stays_open only if the shop is open on that weekday (seed_shop is dropped from Blomsterfesten and Høstfesten: both Sundays); (d) the seed shop restocks 25 carrot seeds a day (was 20).
decisions.why: Measured: fixed 08:00 left Maja's bakery unstaffed 115 minutes, Kløvermynte's shop 67, Brumme's 59; a contest could pay up to 5 x 1,670 g = 8,350 g a year; the Sunday festivals promised an open seed shop the Hours rule closes; 6 x 20 carrot seeds a week left a dedicated 110-plot field 2.1 seeds a day short (-4.8 % income).

decisions.title: Balance claims are ranges in two availability variants; four heart scenes per tier A citizen
decisions.decision: social.balance_claims_hold asserts ranges, not points (median <= 80, p90 <= 115 with LEAN events, <= 110 with four events) in a `free` and a `mixed` variant (visits at mixed hours, keepers reachable at their counters), with a ratchet file written by the first accepted run; S-heart-content builds 40 scenes (4 / 6 / 8 / 10 hearts for the 10 tier A citizens) instead of 20 and becomes size L. The year-2 hook (a new birthday card per year) and the 2-heart introduction stay roadmap.
decisions.why: se6 (100 runs x 336 days): typical tier A to 8 hearts free 71 / p90 97, mixed 70 / 108 with the talk cells; with four events free 66 / 90, mixed 65 / 101; a typical player has seen all 20 LEAN scenes by day 97 (p90) and has 14 of 30 citizens at 10 hearts after a game year.

decisions.title: The loop digest excludes every wall-clock path
decisions.decision: digest_volatile.json lists exactly /game/play_time_seconds, /meta/saved_at, /meta/timestamp and /meta/summary; town_loop.digest_stable_over_wall_clock compares two digests taken 1.1 s apart; l13_digest_has_teeth still proves gold and flags move the digest.
decisions.why: SaveManager.gather_payload writes saved_at and timestamp from the real clock: two gathers 1.1 s apart differed in exactly those two paths and the prototype's two-path list gave two digests (D3/final_editor/te4).

decisions.title: The ownership proof must be usable by the lead's tooling
decisions.decision: check_ownership.py (this folder) can emit the EFFECTIVE owners table (include and exclude patterns per package, all layers merged) with `--emit-effective FILE`; the lead's impl/tools/ownership.py must honour exclusions like the checker does (a drop-in `lead_tools/ownership.py` is shipped); the docstring of the checker no longer claims the old tool has the same semantics.
decisions.why: impl/tools/ownership.py reads only owners[pid]['owns'] and make_orders.py removes by exact string: 67 of 69 ownsRemove entries of this addendum are sub-paths of wider globs, so a regeneration with the old rule leaves them doubly owned and the gate tool accepts it silently.

conflicts.tracks: plan: P11; farm: N01
conflicts.decision: N01 (carve-out; reversible with two lines)

openQuestions.question: A 10-line listening test before the bulk voice bake
openQuestions.context: One Danish system voice (Sara) with 8 pitch / rate presets for 30 characters; the invented names (Kløvermynte, Hasselnød, Hyldeblomst, Rosmarin, Fingerbøl, Stokrose, Bøgeknop) are unverified.

openQuestions.question: The night watch
openQuestions.context: At 23:45 a forced walk home to the farm door (whispered from 23:30, never during a modal) protects you from waking up in a shop. Alternative: none, you pass out where you stand.

openQuestions.question: Two stalls without a room: acceptable?
openQuestions.context: Your requirement says every shop and service is also a room you walk into. The sketch draws the Torvet market stall and the bat house window as outdoor stalls: Torvestanden (Brumme's weekend stall, the same shop id as his workshop room) and Natteblik-vinduet (the map seller, evenings). They are the only two exceptions (24 rooms for 28 non-decor buildings) and their keepers are reachable at the stall ends like at every counter. The alternative is a 3 x 3 room for each (about 2 points of work and one more interior each for the router).
openQuestions.default: the two stalls stay outdoor, the sketch's own form

tasks: scripts/towns/town_marker.gd (class TownMarker) registered in lua/config/marker_handlers.lua (F4 fix-round) for the three types: `@marker T town [curfew=false] [area=<id>]` (ONE per map, returns the TownDirector), `@marker D door building=<id> [interior=<area>]` (a Door2D at the doorstep + the arrival spawn from_int_<building> one cell in front), `@marker P post name=<id> [act=] [cap=] [facing=]` (+ `set=fest spot=<id>` for the 24-post festival set; the marker list is read by T-routes' TownMarks.collect and a post on a blocked cell is snapped by TownMarks.resolve_cells, both defined one wave before this file); every existing `warp` marker is a GATE (its cell becomes the anchor gate_<to area>, linked to gate_<this area> of the area it leads to: no extra marker for a bridge); the map parser takes any single character as the object char (proven with the characters æ, Ø and é), so an author is never short of chars -> verify: towns_director.handlers_registered, towns_director.markers_build_doors_and_spawns, towns_director.unicode_marker_chars, towns_director.collect_posts_gates_fest, towns_director.gates_from_warp_markers, towns_director.post_marker_defaults

scripts/towns/town_director.gd (class TownDirector, a child of the area, created by the `town` marker): lives in the area tree (_exit_tree frees every citizen node: a parked area keeps no sheets), keeps exactly the citizens alive whose body is in this area now (Routines.present_in), spawns them at the carrot position, moves them with move_and_slide (mask world | player | ground_block, NOT layer 4: citizens pass hatches and never block each other), catches up at 1.6 x the leg speed, snaps a follower more than 420 ground px behind, removes one near the door it leaves through, pauses with the clock (PLAYING only), resyncs on area_changed / day_started / each clock minute / a time skip (3 h skip 4-5 ms, overnight 0 outdoors at 06:00), cap towns.max_live_visuals distinct looks with priority order (festival crowd first), game_event area_populated {area, citizens, visuals, dropped}, game_event shop_open_changed for the buildings of the area, game_event routine_changed {hour} on every full game hour while the area is loaded (the `when=at:` / `away:` markers refresh on it); the director also calls NpcDirector.register(self) in _ready and unregister(self) in _exit_tree (NpcDirector finds the live director of an area in its static registry and makes duck-typed calls: post_ground, node_of, population, controls; no `as TownDirector` cast anywhere in wave-5 code); portal legs are 'the citizen is at the far side anchor' -> verify: towns_director.live_equals_wanted_every_hour, towns_director.follower_lag_bounded, towns_director.blocked_doorway_recovers, towns_director.time_skip_resync, towns_director.park_enter_30_cycles_no_leak, towns_director.visual_cap_priority, towns_director.events_area_populated_and_shop_open_changed, towns_director.routine_changed_every_full_hour

tasks: EventRunner (Node child of the SocialManager, one scene at a time): start(event_id) queues and starts ONLY when GameManager.current_phase == PLAYING and no modal is open and the world is not sleeping / traveling (retries on modal_changed and day_started, a queued AUTOMATIC scene is dropped to a toast after 2 game days), pushes the NON-pausing modal `event` (phase CUTSCENE: the clock is frozen, nothing can be saved or slept through), plays steps top to bottom: fade, stand, walk, face, camera, clip, emote, say, choice, give, points, flag, wait, time, sfx, end; consecutive `say` steps of one speaker are ONE DialogueUI run (speaker portrait via TTPortraits), a `choice` step (<= 3 options, each {id, text_key, reply_key, points?, flag?}) becomes the choices of the last page, `give` goes through EconomyManager, `points` through SocialManager.add_points(event), a `time` step advances <= 120 minutes and never past 23:59; heart events are PLAYER-INITIATED: meta.trigger = talk shows the rose heart bubble over the NPC and the choice 'Hvad har du på hjerte?' when hearts, the `when` spec and the once / cooldown rules hold (never a surprise cutscene); rewards are paid ONCE when the scene ends or is skipped; Esc opens UiConfirm 'Spring scenen over?' (default Fortsæt) and a skip FAST-FORWARDS: the remaining give / points / flag steps run at once and choices take option 1 (nothing is lost); seen flags: seen[event] = 1 (heart events) or the year (festival scenes, once per year); events heart_event_started / heart_event_finished {id, npc, hearts} -> verify: social_events.waits_for_playing_and_no_modal, social_events.queue_drops_after_two_days, social_events.steps_vocabulary, social_events.say_runs_merge_per_speaker, social_events.choice_takes_option_one_on_skip, social_events.rewards_paid_once, social_events.skip_fast_forwards_effects, social_events.heart_event_only_on_talk, social_events.seen_once_and_once_per_year, social_events.no_save_or_sleep_during_event

Honest actor control: the runner drives Npc2D / Player2D only through the event API that the P14 and P06 amendments add (event_begin / event_end, event_walk_to(pos, speed) awaitable, event_face, event_clip, camera_focus(target, zoom, seconds) / camera_release); when a method is missing the step is SKIPPED, counted in runner.skipped_directives and the scene still plays its lines (a camera or walk step never blocks a scene); marks are posts of the stage area (mark:<id>) whose positions come from NpcDirector.post_ground(area_id, name) (late bound: the director knows the map markers of Hyggebyen AND the sidecar posts of the city, which has no map text; Vector2.INF = unknown), a missing mark falls back to where the actor stands and the validator rule events.marks_exist fails once the maps exist; actors are released to the routine layer (NpcDirector.resync) when the scene ends -> verify: social_events.missing_actor_api_is_skipped_not_fatal, social_events.marks_exist (SKIP until the maps carry the posts, REQUIRED at the wave-6 gate), social_events.actors_released_on_end

Activity primitives (all festivals compose these six, the only mini-games): contest {select} = the player picks one matching item (the gift grid in contest mode), score = sell value x (1 + 0.5 x rarity rank) x (1 +- 0.15 SocialRng jitter), the three NPC bars of the year are the best value of the category x (0.5, 0.75, 1.0) with the same jitter, rank = bars beaten -> rewards.contest.first|second|third (items of rarity <= rare, never keepsakes, and capped in VALUE by SocialValidator SV14: first <= min(2 x the cheapest winning entry of the category, 400 g), second <= 0.7 x first, third <= 0.4 x first); potluck {select} = donate items to the table, a goal of 12 shared by the town, reward at the finale; wish = choose one of three wishes, a lantern prop lights (when= fest:<id>), +20 points to the host, a flag wish_<id>_<year> (flavour, no perk); feast = restore energy and hearts once per festival; dance = scripted scene with the HIGHEST-hearts citizen present as partner (+30 points, archetype lines FEST_DANCE_<ARCH>); market = ShopSystem.open_shop(def.shop) with the festival stall shops of lua/shops/festival_markets.lua (S-fest-content) -> verify: social_events.contest_is_deterministic_per_seed_and_year, social_events.contest_rewards_never_keepsake, social_events.contest_reward_over_cap_is_refused, social_events.potluck_goal_and_finale, social_events.wish_is_flavour_only, social_events.feast_once_per_festival, social_events.dance_partner_is_highest_hearts, social_events.market_opens_festival_shop
